Now let me write the RCA and plan the TDD fix.

## RCA

**Bug**: `decodeSessionCwd` turns hyphens in directory names into `/`, producing non-existent paths that break mailbox wake for dashed folder names.

**Root cause**: `lib/src/session_repo.dart:110-133` — `_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` to `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses by `inner.split('-').join('/')`. The mapping is many-to-one (lossy): a literal `-` in a path segment is indistinguishable from an encoded separator.

**Impact**:
1. `FileMessagingRepository.directory()` populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with a bogus path for hyphenated workspaces.
2. `_recordRegistry` persists the bogus cwd to `messages-registry.json`.
3. `_launchMailboxWake` (agent_cli) / wake in subagent_tools spawns with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd` → `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — asleep mailbox can never be woken.

**Fix approach**:
1. Make the slug encoding reversible: percent-escape `%`, `/`, `\`, `:` (`%25`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`). Paths without those chars (the overwhelming majority, including all `_`/`.`/`-` names without `%`) produce slugs byte-identical to the legacy scheme, so existing on-disk folders stay decodable. `decodeSessionCwd` decodes reversibly when the slug carries new-format escapes, and falls back to the legacy split for legacy slugs.
2. `_recordRegistry` stores the exact `_env.cwd` (it is the live env at registration time) instead of a lossy slug round-trip.
3. `directory()` prefers the mailbox's exact `cwd` from `messages-registry.json` (keyed by the `.id` marker) and only falls back to slug decode when the registry has no entry.
4. `_launchMailboxWake` verifies the cwd exists (and is a directory) before spawning, returning a clear refusal text instead of a `ProcessException`.

content.text:
## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags

Now, let me think about the design of the fix.

**Root cause**: `_encodeCwd` maps `/`, `\`, `:` → `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that by splitting on `-`. Any literal hyphen in a path is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so the decode is lossy for hyphenated paths.

**Fix approach** (from ticket):
1. Encode slug reversibly — percent-encoding or escaping hyphens as `--`.
2. `directory()` / `_launchMailboxWake` should prefer the exact verified cwd from `messages-registry.json` or verify `Directory(cwd).existsSync()` before spawn.

Consideration 1: backwards compatibility with existing on-disk slugs.

If I change the encode scheme, new sessions go into new-format slug dirs. Old sessions stay in old-format dirs. Session listing reads cwd from the session file header (not the slug), so listing is unaffected. The decode function is only used by the messaging fabric:
- `directory()`: iterates slug dirs under the messages root and decodes names.
- `_recordRegistry()`: decodes the CURRENT env cwd's slug.

Old slug dirs on disk (created by older versions, e.g. `--Users-Yury-postal-nl--`) would decode differently under the new scheme. With percent-encoding decode: `--Users-Yury-postal-nl--` → no `%` escapes → the inner `Users-Yury-postal-nl` treated as one segment → `/Users-Yury-postal-nl`. That's a non-existent path, same brokeness class as before for legacy dirs.

But if decode keeps a legacy fallback: for slugs without any new-format escapes, we could try... no wait — a legacy slug `--Users-Yury-postal-nl--` could be EITHER `/Users/Yury/postal/nl` or `/Users/Yury/postal-nl` or `/Users/Yury-postal/nl`... we cannot know. The decode is fundamentally ambiguous for legacy slugs. That's why the ticket also proposes part 2: consumers should prefer the exact cwd recorded in the registry (which is the real `_env.cwd` string, stored at registration time by `_recordRegistry`... wait, no — `_recordRegistry` itself derives cwd by decoding the slug! That's the same lossy path. Hmm.

```dart
final slug = encodeSessionCwd(_env.cwd);
final cwd = _decodeSessionCwd?.call(slug) ?? '';
``

So the registry's cwd is derived by encode→decode roundtrip of `_env.cwd` — bogus for hyphenated cwds. The obvious fix here: store `_env.cwd` directly! The registry write happens at registration from the live env — `_env.cwd` IS available and exact. So `_recordRegistry` should write `'cwd': _env.cwd` instead of decoding the slug. That's a one-line fix that makes the registry hold the exact cwd. 

Then `directory()` should prefer the registry's exact cwd. But `directory()` iterates slug dirs; for each mailbox dir it knows the mailbox id (via `.id` marker) — it can look up `_registrySlugFor(id)`... wait, `_registrySlugFor` returns the slug, not cwd. Let me re-read:

   return entry['slug'] as String;

}
``

It returns the slug. For directory() we'd want the cwd. I can add a method `_registryCwdFor(agentId)` returning `entry['cwd']`.

But hold on — is `directory()`'s decode fallback needed at all? For mailboxes of instances that never registered in the registry (legacy, or other tools), the slug decode is the only source. So `directory()` logic becomes:

final cwd = registryCwd ?? _decodeSessionCwd?.call(slugDir.name);
``

So the only real `wakeProcess` implementation in the repo is `_launchMailboxWake` in agent_cli.dart (wired at line 559 into `SubagentServices`). 

Now let me write the RCA and plan the TDD fix.

## RCA

**Bug**: `decodeSessionCwd` turns hyphens in directory names into `/`, producing non-existent paths that break mailbox wake for dashed folder names.

**Root cause**: `lib/src/session_repo.dart:110-133` — `_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` to `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses by `inner.split('-').join('/')`. The mapping is many-to-one (lossy): a literal `-` in a path segment is indistinguishable from an encoded separator.

**Impact**:
1. `FileMessagingRepository.directory()` populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with a bogus path for hyphenated workspaces.
2. `_recordRegistry` persists the bogus cwd to `messages-registry.json`.
3. `_launchMailboxWake` (agent_cli) / wake in subagent_tools spawns with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd` → `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — asleep mailbox can never be woken.

**Fix approach**:
1. Make the slug encoding reversible: percent-escape `%`, `/`, `\`, `:` (`%25`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`). Paths without those chars (the overwhelming majority, including all `_`/`.`/`-` names without `%`) produce slugs byte-identical to the legacy scheme, so existing on-disk folders stay decodable. `decodeSessionCwd` decodes reversibly when the slug carries new-format escapes, and falls back to the legacy split for legacy slugs.
2. `_recordRegistry` stores the exact `_env.cwd` (it is the live env at registration time) instead of a lossy slug round-trip.
3. `directory()` prefers the mailbox's exact `cwd` from `messages-registry.json` (keyed by the `.id` marker) and only falls back to slug decode when the registry has no entry.
4. `_launchMailboxWake` verifies the cwd exists (and is a directory) before spawning, returning a clear refusal text instead of a `ProcessException`.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

So the only real `wakeProcess` implementation in the repo is `_launchMailboxWake` in agent_cli.dart (wired at line 559 into `SubagentServices`). 

Now let me write the RCA and plan the TDD fix.

## RCA

**Bug**: `decodeSessionCwd` turns hyphens in directory names into `/`, producing non-existent paths that break mailbox wake for dashed folder names.

**Root cause**: `lib/src/session_repo.dart:110-133` — `_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` to `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses by `inner.split('-').join('/')`. The mapping is many-to-one (lossy): a literal `-` in a path segment is indistinguishable from an encoded separator.

**Impact**:
1. `FileMessagingRepository.directory()` populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with a bogus path for hyphenated workspaces.
2. `_recordRegistry` persists the bogus cwd to `messages-registry.json`.
3. `_launchMailboxWake` (agent_cli) / wake in subagent_tools spawns with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd` → `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — asleep mailbox can never be woken.

**Fix approach**:
1. Make the slug encoding reversible: percent-escape `%`, `/`, `\`, `:` (`%25`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`). Paths without those chars (the overwhelming majority, including all `_`/`.`/`-` names without `%`) produce slugs byte-identical to the legacy scheme, so existing on-disk folders stay decodable. `decodeSessionCwd` decodes reversibly when the slug carries new-format escapes, and falls back to the legacy split for legacy slugs.
2. `_recordRegistry` stores the exact `_env.cwd` (it is the live env at registration time) instead of a lossy slug round-trip.
3. `directory()` prefers the mailbox's exact `cwd` from `messages-registry.json` (keyed by the `.id` marker) and only falls back to slug decode when the registry has no entry.
4. `_launchMailboxWake` verifies the cwd exists (and is a directory) before spawning, returning a clear refusal text instead of a `ProcessException`.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags

Key rules noted:
- `lib/` is pure Dart — NO `dart:io`. All fs via `ExecutionEnv`. My fix must not use dart:io — use `ExecutionEnv.exists`.
- Memory search before non-trivial tasks — let me search memory for relevant facts.
- No UI work — no golden tests needed.
- This is a CI runner checkout (branch `ai/gh-174` created for me), so the "shared checkout" rule doesn't restrict me — the task IS to fix the bug on this branch.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `decodeSessionCwd` irreversibly turns hyphens in directory names into path separators, so mailboxes in hyphenated workspaces (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) report a bogus cwd and the mailbox wake spawn fails.

**Root cause**: `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart` — `_encodeCwd` (line 110) flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-`, and `decodeSessionCwd` (line 124) reverses it with `inner.split('-').join('/')`. The mapping is many-to-one: a literal `-` inside a path segment is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so the decode is lossy for any hyphenated path.

**Impact**:
- `FileMessagingRepository.directory()` (`file_messaging_repository.dart:372`) populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with a non-existent path.
- `_recordRegistry` (`file_messaging_repository.dart:443`) persists that bogus cwd into `~/.fah/messages-registry.json` (it round-trips `_env.cwd` through the lossy slug).
- `_launchMailboxWake` (`agent_cli.dart`, via `subagent_tools.dart:624` `cwd: entry.cwd`) spawns the headless wake run in the non-existent directory → `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken by incoming mail.

**Fix approach** (ticket proposal, both parts):
1. Make the slug reversible: escape the literal `-` as `%2D` (plus `%`→`%25`, `\`→`%5C`, `:`→`%3A`; separators stay `-`). Any path without those characters encodes byte-identically to the legacy scheme, so existing on-disk slug folders and the pi-mono layout stay untouched; `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when the slug carries escapes and falls back to the legacy split otherwise.
2. Make consumers prefer the exact cwd: `_recordRegistry` stores the live `_env.cwd` verbatim instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by the mailbox `.id`) and only falls back to slug decode; `_launchMailboxWake` verifies the cwd exists before spawning and refuses with a clear reason instead of a `ProcessException`.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-174.

So the only real `wakeProcess` implementation in the repo is `_launchMailboxWake` in agent_cli.dart (wired at line 559 into `SubagentServices`). 

Now let me write the RCA and plan the TDD fix.

## RCA

**Bug**: `decodeSessionCwd` turns hyphens in directory names into `/`, producing non-existent paths that break mailbox wake for dashed folder names.

**Root cause**: `lib/src/session_repo.dart:110-133` — `_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` to `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses by `inner.split('-').join('/')`. The mapping is many-to-one (lossy): a literal `-` in a path segment is indistinguishable from an encoded separator.

**Impact**:
1. `FileMessagingRepository.directory()` populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with a bogus path for hyphenated workspaces.
2. `_recordRegistry` persists the bogus cwd to `messages-registry.json`.
3. `_launchMailboxWake` (agent_cli) / wake in subagent_tools spawns with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd` → `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — asleep mailbox can never be woken.

**Fix approach**:
1. Make the slug encoding reversible: percent-escape `%`, `/`, `\`, `:` (`%25`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`). Paths without those chars (the overwhelming majority, including all `_`/`.`/`-` names without `%`) produce slugs byte-identical to the legacy scheme, so existing on-disk folders stay decodable. `decodeSessionCwd` decodes reversibly when the slug carries new-format escapes, and falls back to the legacy split for legacy slugs.
2. `_recordRegistry` stores the exact `_env.cwd` (it is the live env at registration time) instead of a lossy slug round-trip.
3. `directory()` prefers the mailbox's exact `cwd` from `messages-registry.json` (keyed by the `.id` marker) and only falls back to slug decode when the registry has no entry.
4. `_launchMailboxWake` verifies the cwd exists (and is a directory) before spawning, returning a clear refusal text instead of a `ProcessException`.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags

Key rules noted:
- `lib/` is pure Dart — NO `dart:io`. All fs via `ExecutionEnv`. My fix must not use dart:io — use `ExecutionEnv.exists`.
- Memory search before non-trivial tasks — let me search memory for relevant facts.
- No UI work — no golden tests needed.
- This is a CI runner checkout (branch `ai/gh-174` created for me), so the "shared checkout" rule doesn't restrict me — the task IS to fix the bug on this branch.

2. `_recordRegistry` persists the bogus cwd to `messages-registry.json`.
3. `_launchMailboxWake` (agent_cli) / wake in subagent_tools spawns with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd` → `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — asleep mailbox can never be woken.

**Fix approach**:
1. Make the slug encoding reversible: percent-escape `%`, `/`, `\`, `:` (`%25`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`). Paths without those chars (the overwhelming majority, including all `_`/`.`/`-` names without `%`) produce slugs byte-identical to the legacy scheme, so existing on-disk folders stay decodable. `decodeSessionCwd` decodes reversibly when the slug carries new-format escapes, and falls back to the legacy split for legacy slugs.
2. `_recordRegistry` stores the exact `_env.cwd` (it is the live env at registration time) instead of a lossy slug round-trip.
3. `directory()` prefers the mailbox's exact `cwd` from `messages-registry.json` (keyed by the `.id` marker) and only falls back to slug decode when the registry has no entry.
4. `_launchMailboxWake` verifies the cwd exists (and is a directory) before spawning, returning a clear refusal text instead of a `ProcessException`.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags

Key rules noted:
- `lib/` is pure Dart — NO `dart:io`. All fs via `ExecutionEnv`. My fix must not use dart:io — use `ExecutionEnv.exists`.
- Memory search before non-trivial tasks — let me search memory for relevant facts.
- No UI work — no golden tests needed.
- This is a CI runner checkout (branch `ai/gh-174` created for me), so the "shared checkout" rule doesn't restrict me — the task IS to fix the bug on this branch.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `decodeSessionCwd` irreversibly turns hyphens in directory names into path separators, so mailboxes in hyphenated workspaces (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) report a bogus cwd and the mailbox wake spawn fails.

**Root cause**: `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart` — `_encodeCwd` (line 110) flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-`, and `decodeSessionCwd` (line 124) reverses it with `inner.split('-').join('/')`. The mapping is many-to-one: a literal `-` inside a path segment is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so the decode is lossy for any hyphenated path.

**Impact**:
- `FileMessagingRepository.directory()` (`file_messaging_repository.dart:372`) populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with a non-existent path.
- `_recordRegistry` (`file_messaging_repository.dart:443`) persists that bogus cwd into `~/.fah/messages-registry.json` (it round-trips `_env.cwd` through the lossy slug).
- `_launchMailboxWake` (`agent_cli.dart`, via `subagent_tools.dart:624` `cwd: entry.cwd`) spawns the headless wake run in the non-existent directory → `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken by incoming mail.

**Fix approach** (ticket proposal, both parts):
1. Make the slug reversible: escape the literal `-` as `%2D` (plus `%`→`%25`, `\`→`%5C`, `:`→`%3A`; separators stay `-`). Any path without those characters encodes byte-identically to the legacy scheme, so existing on-disk slug folders and the pi-mono layout stay untouched; `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when the slug carries escapes and falls back to the legacy split otherwise.
2. Make consumers prefer the exact cwd: `_recordRegistry` stores the live `_env.cwd` verbatim instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by the mailbox `.id`) and only falls back to slug decode; `_launchMailboxWake` verifies the cwd exists before spawning and refuses with a clear reason instead of a `ProcessException`.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-174.
"}

Now, let me think about the design of the fix.

**Root cause**: `_encodeCwd` maps `/`, `\`, `:` → `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that by splitting on `-`. Any literal hyphen in a path is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so the decode is lossy for hyphenated paths.

**Fix approach** (from ticket):
1. Encode slug reversibly — percent-encoding or escaping hyphens as `--`.
2. `directory()` / `_launchMailboxWake` should prefer the exact verified cwd from `messages-registry.json` or verify `Directory(cwd).existsSync()` before spawn.

Consideration 1: backwards compatibility with existing on-disk slugs.

If I change the encode scheme, new sessions go into new-format slug dirs. Old sessions stay in old-format dirs. Session listing reads cwd from the session file header (not the slug), so listing is unaffected. The decode function is only used by the messaging fabric:
- `directory()`: iterates slug dirs under the messages root and decodes names.
- `_recordRegistry()`: decodes the CURRENT env cwd's slug.

Old slug dirs on disk (created by older versions, e.g. `--Users-Yury-postal-nl--`) would decode differently under the new scheme. With percent-encoding decode: `--Users-Yury-postal-nl--` → no `%` escapes → the inner `Users-Yury-postal-nl` treated as one segment → `/Users-Yury-postal-nl`. That's a non-existent path, same brokeness class as before for legacy dirs.

But if decode keeps a legacy fallback: for slugs without any new-format escapes, we could try... no wait — a legacy slug `--Users-Yury-postal-nl--` could be EITHER `/Users/Yury/postal/nl` or `/Users/Yury/postal-nl` or `/Users/Yury-postal/nl`... we cannot know. The decode is fundamentally ambiguous for legacy slugs. That's why the ticket also proposes part 2: consumers should prefer the exact cwd recorded in the registry (which is the real `_env.cwd` string, stored at registration time by `_recordRegistry`... wait, no — `_recordRegistry` itself derives cwd by decoding the slug! That's the same lossy path. Hmm.

Wait, let me re-read `_recordRegistry`:

```dart
final slug = encodeSessionCwd(_env.cwd);
final cwd = _decodeSessionCwd?.call(slug) ?? '';
``

So the registry's cwd is derived by encode→decode roundtrip of `_env.cwd` — bogus for hyphenated cwds. The obvious fix here: store `_env.cwd` directly! The registry write happens at registration from the live env — `_env.cwd` IS available and exact. So `_recordRegistry` should write `'cwd': _env.cwd` instead of decoding the slug. That's a one-line fix that makes the registry hold the exact cwd. 

Then `directory()` should prefer the registry's exact cwd. But `directory()` iterates slug dirs; for each mailbox dir it knows the mailbox id (via `.id` marker) — it can look up `_registrySlugFor(id)`... wait, `_registrySlugFor` returns the slug, not cwd. Let me re-read:

```dart
Future<String?> _registrySlugFor(String agentId) async {
 ...
 final entry = decoded[agentId];
 if (entry is Map<String, dynamic> && entry['slug'] is String) {
   return entry['slug'] as String;
 }
 ...
}
``

It returns the slug. For directory() we'd want the cwd. I can add a method `_registryCwdFor(agentId)` returning `entry['cwd']`.

But hold on — is `directory()`'s decode fallback needed at all? For mailboxes of instances that never registered in the registry (legacy, or other tools), the slug decode is the only source. So `directory()` logic becomes:

```dart
final cwd = registryCwd ?? _decodeSessionCwd?.call(slugDir.name);
``

Hmm wait, but should we also verify existence? The ticket says "prefer the exact verified cwd stored in messages-registry.json or verify Directory(cwd).existsSync() before attempting process spawn". The registry cwd is written from `_env.cwd` (exact), so it's trustworthy. Verification of existence in directory() may be too aggressive (a registry cwd might legitimately not exist after the folder was moved/deleted; then the decode fallback or null would be fine).

For the wake path in `subagent_tools.dart:624` (`cwd: entry.cwd ?? '.'`), and `agent_cli.dart`'s `_launchMailboxWake` — the ticket says "verify Directory(cwd).existsSync() before attempting process spawn". Let me look at what happens today: `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — where does that surface? `_launchMailboxWake` in agent_cli uses `_env.exec(command, options: ShellExecOptions(cwd: cwd))`. And subagent_tools launcher is `manager.wakeProcess`. Let me check how wakeProcess is wired in subagent manager and in the app host.

Actually, wait. Let me focus. The core fix per the ticket:

1. **Reversible slug encoding** — fix `encodeSessionCwd`/`decodeSessionCwd` so roundtrip is lossless.
2. **directory()** — prefer exact registry cwd.
3. **_recordRegistry** — store the real cwd.
4. **Wake path** — verify existence before spawn.

Now, about the encoding scheme choice. The slug must be a valid single directory name. Options:

**Option A: percent-encoding** — encode `/`, `\`, `:` (and `%`) as `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`, `%25`. Decode: unescape. Roundtrip exact. Old slugs decode via legacy fallback.

Wait — but what about hyphens under percent-encoding? They don't need escaping at all. `%` needs escaping to make decode unambiguous (a legacy path containing `%2F` literally... e.g. cwd `/tmp/a%2Fb` encoded legacy = `--tmp-a%2Fb--` which new decode would unescape to `/tmp/a/b` — wrong). So escape `%` → `%25`. 

**Option B: escape hyphens as `--`** — separators stay `-`, hyphens become `--`. Decode: scan tokens. `--` is the wrap marker though! The slug is wrapped in leading/trailing `--`. Inner `--` escaping: decode needs to distinguish `-` (separator) from `--` (literal hyphen). But wait: `--foo--` wrapped, inner = `foo`. A path `/a--b/c` would encode to inner `a----b-c`... hmm, and `/a-/b`? inner `a---b-c`? Ambiguity arises: `a---b` could be `a` + sep + `-b` (hyphen-escaped?) no wait, in this scheme a literal `-` in path stays `-`? No — scheme B: separators (`/`, `\`, `:`) → `-`, literal hyphens → `--`. Then `/a-/b` → `a---b` (a, sep→-, hyphen→--, b). And `/a--b/c` → `a----b-c`. Decode: split is deterministic left-to-right: `-` = separator, `--` = literal hyphen. `a---b` → `a` sep `-b`? Scanning: `a`, then `-` followed by `-` → literal `-`, then `b`... wait `a---b`: scan from left: `a`; see `--` → literal hyphen; then `-b`? next char after the two is `-`, that's a separator, then `b`. Result: `a-b`... hmm no. Let me be careful:

`/a-/b` → components: `a`, `-`, `b`... wait no, `/a-/b` path segments are `a-` and `b`. Encode: `a` + `-`(sep) + `-`→`--` + `-`(sep) + `b` = `a---b`. Decode scanning left to right: `a`; `--` → literal hyphen `-`; `-` → separator; `b` → `a` `-` sep `b` → segments `a-` and `b`. Correct!

But `a---b` could also decode as `a` `-`(sep) `--`(hyphen) `b` → segments `a` and `-b` → `/a/-b`. Scanning left-to-right greedily gives the first. Is greedy left-to-right unambiguous? In prefix codes yes, and this IS a prefix code ({`-`, `--`} — neither is a prefix of the other... wait `-` IS a prefix of `--`! A code where one codeword is a prefix of another is not instantaneously decodable left-to-right without lookahead... but with lookahead of one char it IS decodable: when you see `-`, peek next char: if `-` then it's a literal hyphen (consume both), else separator. That's a valid one-symbol-lookahead decoder. Is it uniquely decodable? Consider encoded string `x--y`: could be `x` + hyphen + `y` (segments `x-y`), OR `x` + sep + `-y`? For the latter, the encoding would be `x-` + `--` + `y` = `x---y`. Different string. OR `x-` + sep + `y` = `x--y` — uh oh! Path segments `x-` and `y` encode to `x` + `-`(literal hyphen in segment) + `-`(sep) + `y` = `x--y`. And path segments `x`, `-y`: `x` + `-`(sep) + `--`(literal hyphen) + `y` = `x---y`. OK so `x--y` uniquely decodes greedily as `x` `-y`→ wait greedy: at `x`, then see `-` with next `-` → literal hyphen, then `y`. Result: segment `x-y`. But the true encoding was segments `x-`, `y` → decode should be `/x-/y`. GREDY FAILS!

Hmm: segments `x-`, `y`: encode each literal hyphen as `--`, each separator as `-`: `x` `--` `-` `y` → `x---y`? No wait: segment `x-` = `x` + hyphen → `x--`; separator → `-`; segment `y` → `y`. Tota…

So the only real `wakeProcess` implementation in the repo is `_launchMailboxWake` in agent_cli.dart (wired at line 559 into `SubagentServices`). 

Now let me write the RCA and plan the TDD fix.

## RCA

**Bug**: `decodeSessionCwd` turns hyphens in directory names into `/`, producing non-existent paths that break mailbox wake for dashed folder names.

**Root cause**: `lib/src/session_repo.dart:110-133` — `_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` to `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses by `inner.split('-').join('/')`. The mapping is many-to-one (lossy): a literal `-` in a path segment is indistinguishable from an encoded separator.

**Impact**:
1. `FileMessagingRepository.directory()` populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with a bogus path for hyphenated workspaces.
2. `_recordRegistry` persists the bogus cwd to `messages-registry.json`.
3. `_launchMailboxWake` (agent_cli) / wake in subagent_tools spawns with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd` → `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — asleep mailbox can never be woken.

**Fix approach**:
1. Make the slug encoding reversible: percent-escape `%`, `/`, `\`, `:` (`%25`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`). Paths without those chars (the overwhelming majority, including all `_`/`.`/`-` names without `%`) produce slugs byte-identical to the legacy scheme, so existing on-disk folders stay decodable. `decodeSessionCwd` decodes reversibly when the slug carries new-format escapes, and falls back to the legacy split for legacy slugs.
2. `_recordRegistry` stores the exact `_env.cwd` (it is the live env at registration time) instead of a lossy slug round-trip.
3. `directory()` prefers the mailbox's exact `cwd` from `messages-registry.json` (keyed by the `.id` marker) and only falls back to slug decode when the registry has no entry.
4. `_launchMailboxWake` verifies the cwd exists (and is a directory) before spawning, returning a clear refusal text instead of a `ProcessException`.

Now TDD: first write failing reproduction tests.

Test 1 (session_repo_test.dart): round-trip a hyphenated path:
```dart
test('round-trips paths containing hyphens (gh-174)', () {
 expect(
   decodeSessionCwd(encodeSessionCwd('/Users/u/_w/postal-nl')),
   '/Users/u/_w/postal-nl',
 );
});
``
Currently FAILS (returns `/Users/u/_w/postal/nl`).

Also keep the legacy pinned tests passing:
- `decodeSessionCwd('--Users-Uladzimir_Klyshevich-git-dm.ai--')` → `/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/dm.ai` — legacy fallback preserves this.
- `decodeSessionCwd(encodeSessionCwd('/foo/bar'))` → `/foo/bar` — new encode of `/foo/bar` = `--foo-bar--` (no escapes) → legacy split → `/foo/bar`. 
- `decodeSessionCwd('---foo---')` → null: inner `-foo-`, contains no valid escape → legacy → parts ['', 'foo', '] → null. Good.
- `decodeSessionCwd('--Users')`, `'Users--'`, `'--'`, `''` → null (guard unchanged).

Test 2 (file_messaging_repository_test.dart): `_recordRegistry` writes exact cwd for a hyphenated workspace; `directory()` prefers the registry cwd.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags

- `lib/` is pure Dart — NO `dart:io`. All fs via `ExecutionEnv`. My fix must not use dart:io — use `ExecutionEnv.exists`.

- No UI work — no golden tests needed.
- This is a CI runner checkout (branch `ai/gh-174` created for me), so the "shared checkout" rule doesn't restrict me — the task IS to fix the bug on this branch.

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: `decodeSessionCwd` irreversibly turns hyphens in directory names into path separators, so mailboxes in hyphenated workspaces (e.g. `/Users/Yury_Bakhmutski/_w/postal-nl`) report a bogus cwd and the mailbox wake spawn fails.

**Root cause**: `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart` — `_encodeCwd` (line 110) flattens `/`, `\`, `:` into `-`, and `decodeSessionCwd` (line 124) reverses it with `inner.split('-').join('/')`. The mapping is many-to-one: a literal `-` inside a path segment is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so the decode is lossy for any hyphenated path.

**Impact**:
- `FileMessagingRepository.directory()` (`file_messaging_repository.dart:372`) populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with a non-existent path.
- `_recordRegistry` (`file_messaging_repository.dart:443`) persists that bogus cwd into `~/.fah/messages-registry.json` (it round-trips `_env.cwd` through the lossy slug).
- `_launchMailboxWake` (`agent_cli.dart`, via `subagent_tools.dart:624` `cwd: entry.cwd`) spawns the headless wake run in the non-existent directory → `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — an asleep mailbox can never be woken by incoming mail.

**Fix approach** (ticket proposal, both parts):
1. Make the slug reversible: escape the literal `-` as `%2D` (plus `%`→`%25`, `\`→`%5C`, `:`→`%3A`; separators stay `-`). Any path without those characters encodes byte-identically to the legacy scheme, so existing on-disk slug folders and the pi-mono layout stay untouched; `decodeSessionCwd` unescapes per segment when the slug carries escapes and falls back to the legacy split otherwise.
2. Make consumers prefer the exact cwd: `_recordRegistry` stores the live `_env.cwd` verbatim instead of a lossy slug round-trip; `directory()` prefers the registry's exact cwd (keyed by the mailbox `.id`) and only falls back to slug decode; `_launchMailboxWake` verifies the cwd exists before spawning and refuses with a clear reason instead of a `ProcessException`.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-174.
"}

blocks.text:
Now, let me think about the design of the fix.

**Root cause**: `_encodeCwd` maps `/`, `\`, `:` → `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses that by splitting on `-`. Any literal hyphen in a path is indistinguishable from an encoded separator, so the decode is lossy for hyphenated paths.

**Fix approach** (from ticket):
1. Encode slug reversibly — percent-encoding or escaping hyphens as `--`.
2. `directory()` / `_launchMailboxWake` should prefer the exact verified cwd from `messages-registry.json` or verify `Directory(cwd).existsSync()` before spawn.

Consideration 1: backwards compatibility with existing on-disk slugs.

If I change the encode scheme, new sessions go into new-format slug dirs. Old sessions stay in old-format dirs. Session listing reads cwd from the session file header (not the slug), so listing is unaffected. The decode function is only used by the messaging fabric:
- `directory()`: iterates slug dirs under the messages root and decodes names.
- `_recordRegistry()`: decodes the CURRENT env cwd's slug.

Old slug dirs on disk (created by older versions, e.g. `--Users-Yury-postal-nl--`) would decode differently under the new scheme. With percent-encoding decode: `--Users-Yury-postal-nl--` → no `%` escapes → the inner `Users-Yury-postal-nl` treated as one segment → `/Users-Yury-postal-nl`. That's a non-existent path, same brokeness class as before for legacy dirs.

But if decode keeps a legacy fallback: for slugs without any new-format escapes, we could try... no wait — a legacy slug `--Users-Yury-postal-nl--` could be EITHER `/Users/Yury/postal/nl` or `/Users/Yury/postal-nl` or `/Users/Yury-postal/nl`... we cannot know. The decode is fundamentally ambiguous for legacy slugs. That's why the ticket also proposes part 2: consumers should prefer the exact cwd recorded in the registry (which is the real `_env.cwd` string, stored at registration time by `_recordRegistry`... wait, no — `_recordRegistry` itself derives cwd by decoding the slug! That's the same lossy path. Hmm.

Wait, let me re-read `_recordRegistry`:

```dart
final slug = encodeSessionCwd(_env.cwd);
final cwd = _decodeSessionCwd?.call(slug) ?? '';
``

So the registry's cwd is derived by encode→decode roundtrip of `_env.cwd` — bogus for hyphenated cwds. The obvious fix here: store `_env.cwd` directly! The registry write happens at registration from the live env — `_env.cwd` IS available and exact. So `_recordRegistry` should write `'cwd': _env.cwd` instead of decoding the slug. That's a one-line fix that makes the registry hold the exact cwd. 

Then `directory()` should prefer the registry's exact cwd. But `directory()` iterates slug dirs; for each mailbox dir it knows the mailbox id (via `.id` marker) — it can look up `_registrySlugFor(id)`... wait, `_registrySlugFor` returns the slug, not cwd. Let me re-read:

```dart
Future<String?> _registrySlugFor(String agentId) async {
 ...
 final entry = decoded[agentId];
 if (entry is Map<String, dynamic> && entry['slug'] is String) {
   return entry['slug'] as String;
 }
 ...
}
``

It returns the slug. For directory() we'd want the cwd. I can add a method `_registryCwdFor(agentId)` returning `entry['cwd']`.

But hold on — is `directory()`'s decode fallback needed at all? For mailboxes of instances that never registered in the registry (legacy, or other tools), the slug decode is the only source. So `directory()` logic becomes:

```dart
final cwd = registryCwd ?? _decodeSessionCwd?.call(slugDir.name);
``

So the only real `wakeProcess` implementation in the repo is `_launchMailboxWake` in agent_cli.dart (wired at line 559 into `SubagentServices`). 

Now let me write the RCA and plan the TDD fix.

## RCA

**Bug**: `decodeSessionCwd` turns hyphens in directory names into `/`, producing non-existent paths that break mailbox wake for dashed folder names.

**Root cause**: `lib/src/session_repo.dart:110-133` — `_encodeCwd` flattens `/`, `\`, `:` to `-` and `decodeSessionCwd` reverses by `inner.split('-').join('/')`. The mapping is many-to-one (lossy): a literal `-` in a path segment is indistinguishable from an encoded separator.

**Impact**:
1. `FileMessagingRepository.directory()` populates `MailboxEntry.cwd` with a bogus path for hyphenated workspaces.
2. `_recordRegistry` persists the bogus cwd to `messages-registry.json`.
3. `_launchMailboxWake` (agent_cli) / wake in subagent_tools spawns with `workingDirectory: entry.cwd` → `ProcessException: No such file or directory` — asleep mailbox can never be woken.

**Fix approach**:
1. Make the slug encoding reversible: percent-escape `%`, `/`, `\`, `:` (`%25`, `%2F`, `%5C`, `%3A`). Paths without those chars (the overwhelming majority, including all `_`/`.`/`-` names without `%`) produce slugs byte-identical to the legacy scheme, so existing on-disk folders stay decodable. `decodeSessionCwd` decodes reversibly when the slug carries new-format escapes, and falls back to the legacy split for legacy slugs.
2. `_recordRegistry` stores the exact `_env.cwd` (it is the live env at registration time) instead of a lossy slug round-trip.
3. `directory()` prefers the mailbox's exact `cwd` from `messages-registry.json` (keyed by the `.id` marker) and only falls back to slug decode when the registry has no entry.
4. `_launchMailboxWake` verifies the cwd exists (and is a directory) before spawning, returning a clear refusal text instead of a `ProcessException`.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
